scarface rispoli.name: Scarface Rispoli
scarface rispoli.origin: Scarface Rispoli was a notorious mobster who operated out of Groton City. In 1941, he was approached by the Deviant Warlord Kro who was posing as "Mr. S Devile". He convinced Rispoli to cause a series of subway crashes using specially made "Death Boxes" that not only caused the subway trains to crash but kill all passengers aboard. The series of fatal crashes attracted the attention of the Eternal Makkari who was operating as the costumed hero known as Hurricane at the time. As Hurricane, Makkari tracked the "Death Boxes" to the hideout of Rispoli and captured him. Learning who was providing Scarface with the "Death Boxes", Hurricane dumped Rispoli and his men off with the police before clashing with Kro, sending his old enemy into retreat.
weapons: Scarface Rispoli had access to so-called "Death Boxes". Black Boxes comprised of Deviant technology that when planted in the ground near a subway train would cause the train to crash and kill all passengers aboard.

scarlet fasinera.name: Scarlet Fasinera
scarlet fasinera.origin: Abused by her father, Scarlet had an unhappy childhood. One evening when she had had enough of it, she secretly killed her father by lighting his bed with a cigarette. His death was considered an accident, and Scarlet was sent to her aunt and uncle where her living conditions were improved. She became a nun and married Vince Fasinera. He was a small-time criminal who was the second man in her life who mistreated her. He died after falling down the stairs of a church. Adopting the alias of Stained Glass Scarlet, she later became a vigilante after being forced to kill her criminal son, Joseph "Mad Dog" Fasinera. Scarlet was killed resisting arrest in the same church where both her son and husband had died. She gained a cult following after her passing, with a legend spreading that one could pray to her for retribution against wrongdoers. The power of her legend and worship apotheosized Stained Glass Scarlet into a divine entity that lurked the church where she died. True to the legend, people could pray to her to kill. The sudden appearance of bodies killed by Fasinera's modus operandi led to the vigilante Hunter's Moon to investigate her church and come into contact with her. He summoned his master, Khonshu, and the elder god subdued her metaphysically, taking advantage of the fact that she was a newer godling to overpower her.

scarzi bragg.name: Scarzi Bragg
scarzi bragg.origin: Scarzi Bragg was a notorious gambler, racketeer, and murderer who was active in Chicago during the 1940s. When the authorities were closing in on him in 1945, Scarzi fled the country with all the loot his gang had stolen, leaving his minions high and dry. Scarzi then relocated to the Central American town of Chorrera, which had just recently elected a new leader named Ramirez. Scarzi managed to gain Ramirez's confidence and then murdered him. Then he used Ramirez's regime to raise taxes and create a state of martial law that saw its people brutalized and pushed into poverty. When the Human Torch and Toro were discovered to be vacationing in the area, former political leader Don Rodriquez came, asking them to investigate Scarzi and why Ramriez had not been seen since Scarzi arrived in town. The Torch and Toro traveled to Chicago to learn of Bragg's background and enlisted his former gang in helping the locals remove Scarzi's influence from the town. When the two heroes returned to Chorrera, they issued a radio challenge for Ramirez to address his people. Then he used Ramirez's regime to raise taxes and create a state of martial law that saw its people brutalized and pushed into poverty. When the Human Torch and Toro were discovered to be vacationing in the area, former political leader Don Rodriquez came, asking them to investigate Scarzi and why Ramriez had not been seen since Scarzi arrived in town. scheherazade.name: Scheherazade
scheherazade.origin: Centuries ago, Scheherazade was the brilliant and courageous daughter of a Vizier serving King Shahryar. To save both her father and the remaining maidens of the kingdom, she willingly married the king, who had developed the habit of executing his brides after a single night. Through her intelligence and gift for storytelling, Scheherazade captivated Shahryar with tales such as those of Ali Baba, Aladdin, and Sinbad, delaying her execution night after night until the king ultimately abandoned his cruelty and spared her life permanently. Their adventures and legends were eventually compiled into the famous collection known as the Thousand and One Nights. At some later point in history, Scheherazade was abducted by the cosmic being known as the Collector and imprisoned aboard his immense museum-like starship as part of his living collection. Though still youthful in appearance thanks to the ship’s life-preserving technology, she endured centuries of captivity, repeatedly forced to entertain her captor with stories while confined within an Arabian-themed chamber surrounded by force fields. In modern times, Scheherazade encountered Bruce Banner after he too became a prisoner of the Collector. Initially mistaking Banner for another tormentor expecting amusement from her, she angrily rejected him before realizing he was also captive aboard the vessel. Discovering that Banner could still move freely through portions of the ship, Scheherazade and the surrounding prisoners pleaded with him to help them escape. Banner's attempt to free the captives led to a confrontation with the Collector and ultimately triggered his transformation into the Hulk. During the chaos that followed, Hulk destroyed the systems maintaining the prison force fields, unleashing the Collector's captives. Recognizing Hulk as Banner, Scheherazade persuaded the green giant to lead the prisoners to freedom, and together they escaped the spacecraft near Omegaville, Florida. Freedom, however, proved tragically brief. The technology aboard the Collector’s ship had preserved the prisoners from aging for centuries, and once outside its influence their true ages rapidly caught up with them. One after another, the liberated captives withered into dust within minutes. As she herself began to perish, Scheherazade comforted the grieving Hulk by assuring him that death in freedom was preferable to eternal imprisonment. Soon afterward, the abandoned vessel and the remains of its prisoners vanished beneath the explosive overgrowth of vegetation spreading through the swamps around Omegaville.

schoolmaster.name: Schoolmaster
schoolmaster.origin: thumb|left|Sanderson Sanderson was a business partner with real estate tycoon John W. Carver. Together, they built the Greystone Building in New York City. However, Carver betrayed Sanderson and trapped him in a secret room in the top floor of the building and left him to die in 1944. Finding a means to escape the room, Sanderson then secretly began creating "accidents" in the building that left the business tenants to believe that the building was cursed and those who were not injured, maimed, or killed in the building soon broke their leases and left making the venture a flop. Sanderson, wearing a costume and dubbing himself the "Schoolmaster", then began training crooks on the art of killing from his secret room. When John Carver decided to investigate the building's supposed curse, he stumbled upon the Schoolmaster who promptly tossed him from the stop story window, sending Carver falling to his death. While the authorities considered the death a suicide, Carver's widow had her doubts. Hearing these doubts prompted Captain America and Bucky to investigate. They stumbled across the secret room where the Schoolmaster was teaching a class, but some of the villains minions caught the two heroes off guard. The Schoolmaster then put nooses around their necks and attempted to hang the two heroes. Cap and Bucky managed to break free and subdued the Schoolmaster's pupils and chased after the killer. During the fight, Captain America lunged at the Schoolmaster who evaded the Cap, sending him through a window. Cap managed to save himself thanks to a flagpole outside, and he soon confronted the Schoolmaster before he could harm Bucky. Defeated, the Schoolmaster was unmasked and he explained his story to Cap and Bucky. After providing them with the tale, Sanderson then threw himself out a window and fell to his death.
weapons: Sanderson carried two pistols.

schuyler belial.name: Schuyler Belial
schuyler belial.origin: Schuyler Belial was the leader of a Satanist group the Followers of the Left Hand Path. Known as Morning Star, he and his cult spent a year tracking down the Werewolf, Jack Russell, whose blood Belial thought could be used to "revitalize" his followers by turning them into werewolves. In Los Angeles, the cult captured Russell, who escaped shortly after, but not before the cult had implanted a tracking chip in his skull. Russell fled to New York City, where Moon Knight attempted to aid him. They were both later captured by the Cult, and taken to Belial's penthouse at the Tishman Building, at 666 Fifth Avenue. Belial planned to use Moon Knight as a human sacrifice, and then have his followers drink the blood of the Werewolf to give them "the power of the Beast". However, they escaped and Belial sent his followers to retrieve the two, but the cultists were defeated with ease. Moon Knight and Russell later infiltrated the cult, returning to Belial's offices, where they defeated the rest followers. During the fight Russell threw Belial from the roof of the 41st floor to his death. left|thumb At Club Jugular, Morning Star told Hannibal King where to look for the Amulets of Damballah.

schuyler van wickham.name: Schuyler Van Wickham
schuyler van wickham.origin: The Young Allies are meeting at their club house and are waiting for Jeff to show up. Suddenly, Jeff shows up unkempt and acting rude to his fellow team mates angering them. As it turns out, Jeff is attempting to gain membership in the Beta Theta fraternity at his private school. As part of his initiation he has been instructed to be rude to people until 3:30 that afternoon, they send Schuyler Van Wickham to keep an eye on him to make sure he sticks to his initiation task. After leaving the Young Allies club house, Schuyler tells Jeff that he has to be rude to a pair of strangers. Jeff kicks them in the knees, starting a fight. Seeing this, the Young Allies rush to his aid. After the men are fought off, Jeff continues to insult the Young Allies, and Bucky angrily throws him off the team. The men who Jeff attacked turn out to be Terror Tate and his gang, who recognize Schuyler as the son as one of the most wealthy families in town. Tate and his men capture Schuyler, and Jeff jumps onto the back of their car and follows them back to their hideout. Needing help, Jeff rushes out to the Young Allies headquarters. When they refuse to believe his story, he angers them enough to get the team to chase after him. He leads them to Tate's hideout where they realize the truth and easily trounce Tate and his men. With Schuyler free and the 3:30 deadline passing, Jeff is able to explain his actions and the Young Allies welcome him back onto the team.

scorchers hazards.origin: The Scorchers are flame-like creatures who are the air faction of the Habit Hazards. Usually fights occur between them and the other two groups, the Blocker Bots and the Sappers, but they decided to work together by draining every kind of energy from New York City in order to open a portal to another dimension, hoping to release one of the greater powered Hazards who was banished from Earth. As their plan was working out in their favor, they were thwarted by members of Habit Heroes, and the armored Avenger, Iron Man. In retaliation, the Scorchers combined with the other hazards to form a giant gestalt being but they were to late as Iron Man and the Heroes combined all their powers into one to destroy the giant and also prevented the other hazard from coming through the portal by closing it.
weaknesses: Scorchers do not get along with their other hazard brethren.

scorpio ecliptic.name: Scorpio (Ecliptic)
scorpio ecliptic.origin: Scorpio was the founder/leader of the latest incarnation of Zodiac, a terrorist group. Hired by an unknown faction of Department H, Scorpio led his group in framing a militant Separatist group for chemical warfare until the new Alpha Flight intervened. In the ensuing battle, Zodiac member, Virgo, whom Scorpio was apparently in love with, disappeared while in battle with Alpha Flight member Murmur. In an act of retaliation, Scorpio knocked Madison Jeffries unconscious and kidnapped him. Later, Scorpio led a much larger version of Zodiac, to attack Department H. The team killed many Epsilons, and Sasquatch II. They also set an bomb in the nuclear reactor core. It was also revealed that Scorpio "converted" Madison Jeffries into the Zodiac member Gemini. All this in search of the experimental Nth Projector, which they were successful in stealing.

fields.notes: According to Alpha Flight Vol 2 1 (August, 1997), this version of Scorpio was not always a villain. He was once somebody else, and some would say he was a hero. He was a noble soul with great aspirations who has by this time fallen very far. His past identity was a closely kept secret. Despite this hint of his past, his identity was never revealed. The Ecliptic is credited with revealing his true self to him. The implication seems to be that she is responsible for his transformation into a villain. The narration of Alpha Flight Vol 2 1 (August, 1997) hints that Scorpio has a secret agenda which he hides from the other members of the Zodiac. Reportedly if his four original recruits knew the full details of his plan, they would leave the team. Scorpio is very protective of Virgo and does not trust the other members of the Zodiac with her safety. This was the original hint that he is in love with her. Scorpio trusts the Ecliptic and she has used this trust to her benefit. She threatens to quit the team and find another employer if Scorpio fails to follow her instructions. The threat had an effect on him. While in costume, Scorpio's eyes are red. It is unclear if he has a different eye color when out of costume.

Along with her 40,000 scorpion offspring, she wanders the corridors of Hell in search of stray demons to consume. Occasionally, displaced human souls find their way into the Scorpion Queen's domain. The Queen of Hell, Satana, once journeyed to the Scorpion Queen's domain in order to recover the soul of a man named Jason Silence. During her battle with the Scorpion Queen, Satana mercilessly destroyed many of her adversary's brood. She rescued Jason's soul and brought him back to Earth.

scotius sumerisle.name: Scotius Sumerisle
scotius sumerisle.origin: As a young boy, Scotius worked on boats until it was revealed that he was Witchbreed. He was attacked and branded by the fearful populace and very nearly killed. Eventually, however he was found by Carlos Javier and became a pupil at his school. Here he met Jean Grey and they fell in love, though they could not act on it as Jean had to pretend to be a man. On one mission for Javier, Scotius and fellow student Roberto rescued Werner from the Inquisition. When Werner started a friendship with Jean, Scotius became jealous and angry with him. Even as the students were captured, and then preparing to fight in Latveria the two men argued. When Jean's overexertion left her dying, Werner asked Scotius how "he" was doing and Scotius yelled at him and told him to stop the pretense. When he saw how surprised Werner was, he realized that he really did not know she had been a woman. Upon reaching Roanoke, Scotius attempted to apologize to Werner, but was told it was unnecessary because, though he did not realize Grey was a woman, Werner did believe he had feelings for her. Scotius remained in Roanoke with the others after the world had been saved.

scott dakei.name: Scott Dakei
scott dakei.origin: Scott Dakei was a major newspaper publisher and network owner whose ultra conservative anti-mutant views have put him in a paranoid state to the point where he has hidden himself and his daughter Georgia along with bodyguards in a impenetrable fortress he has dubbed the Bunker in New Mexico. He came to the attention of X-Factor when his daughter released a live feed by computer about being trapped within the compound and not being able to experience life, high school, things normal teenagers deal with on a daily basis. Dakei caught her doing the feed and had his bodyguard shoot the computer monitor with a gun. X-Factor arrived at Dakei's front door in their civilian disguise to investigate the incident, but Danger made things worse by stating to Dakei's security system that they were X-Factor, a group of mutants, which they got a negative response with multiple machine guns shooting at them which apparently killed them. Dakei and his bodyguard then came outside to notice the bodies until they all of a sudden disappeared, which was actually Danger using her hard light images to create holograms for a distraction so they could sneak into the place. Dakei, along with a group of men head to his daughter's room to engage them only to witness the body of Cypher laid out on the ground.

scott gaines.name: Scott Gaines
scott gaines.origin: Scotty was the younger brother of Al Gaines, Nuke of the Squadron Supreme and the youngest son of Gilbert and Florence Gaines. Al blamed himself for his beloved parents contracting cancer and dying from it as quickly as they did. Out of concern for his younger brother, and only living relative, Al left Scotty with family friends and almost completely abandoned him in the hope that he would live a long life. After being missing from the Squadron Supreme, Doctor Spectrum came looking for Nuke but found Scotty instead. Scotty told him that his brother was acting weird after the deaths of their parents and took him to the cemetery where the pair were buried and found Al grieving at the graves in the middle of the night. Al was not happy to see his teammate bring his brother to him, mostly because he had kept his dual identity hidden from him and he was afraid Scotty would blame him for the death of their parents, practically drove himself mad with grief and attacked Doctor Spectrum. Scotty watched as the two battled before running off as instructed by Doctor Spectrum. Fearing that he would hurt Nuke, Doctor Spectrum encased him in bubble so that his radiation power wouldn't hurt any innocent bystanders and fly them away from the town. When Doctor Spectrum opened the bubble to confront his friend, he found that Al had burned up his entire supply of oxygen and had suffocated to death. Guilt ridden, Doctor Spectrum later forced himself to return and tell Scotty what happened to his brother. Scotty Gaines was killed along with the other natives of Earth when this reality was destroyed.
powers: No known paranormal ability

family: Gilbert Gaines (father, deceased) Flo Gaines (mother, deceased) Albert Gaines (Nuke) (brother, deceased)

scott hoskins.name: Scott Hoskins
scott hoskins.origin: Scott Hoskins worked for the Super-Crimes Division of the National Security Administration. He entered a secret facility of the NSA to interrogate Bullseye. Hoskins and his team were the ones who captured Bullseye. All seven other members of his team were killed in the effort. While interrogating Bullseye, he continued to taught them as he had stolen nuclear weapons, removing their plutonium cores. While beating him up, he dislodged Bullseye's tooth loose, so Bullseye used his own tooth as a projectile, firing it through Hoskins' skull, killing him.

scott summers clone.name: Scott Summers (Clone)
scott summers clone.species: Altered clone of Scott Summers with both Mutant and Inhuman DNA; empowered by TerrigenesisCategory:Mutant/Inhuman Hybrids
scott summers clone.origin: When the Terrigen Mist was discovered to be toxic to mutants, Mister Sinister began experimenting on unwilling subjects, trying to make Inhuman and mutant DNA co-exist in order to allow the creation of a genetically superior species of mutants; however, the only test subject to survive was a clone of Cyclops. When the X-Men confronted Sinister for kidnapping Nightcrawler, Magik, and Colossus, Sinister was forced to deploy the Cyclops clone to defeat them. thumb|left|The clone's original form At first, the X-Men mistook the clone for the real Cyclops, who had allegedly been killed months ago in a battle against Inhumans, but the time-displaced Jean Grey read his mind and confirmed that the clone wasn't the real Cyclops. The X-Men fought the Cyclops clone, who was overtaken by his Inhuman DNA and mutated into a mindless monster. Logan was able to defeat it with his claws, though the clone continued becoming more and more unstable, to the point where even Mister Sinister noted it is on the verge of exploding. Storm and Jean Grey used their powers to move the clone's unstable body away from the populated area, and once it was far enough away, they allowed it to explode.
powers: as well as those granted by Inhuman physiology including: Armored Body
weaknesses: The clone became mentally unstable as the Inhuman portion of his DNA took over the mutant portion of his DNA. He also became unstable at the genetic level, which ultimately led to his death by explosion.

scotty mcdowell.name: Scotty McDowell
scotty mcdowell.origin: A child prodigy, Scotty McDowell always wanted to become a crimefighter. He had ambitions to join the Federal Bureau of Investigation, but he had an accident which irreversibly paralyzed his legs. Suddenly wheelchair-bound, he discovered that his dream of joining the FBI was out of reach. Settling in Los Angeles, McDowell became an accomplished criminologist, scholarly so that the wheelchair hindered him as little as possible: He convinced his landlady Mrs. Archer to adapt the access of his ground-floor apartment with a ramp on the stairs for his wheelchair, and he had his car modified to drive it manually without using the feet. He filled his home with specialized criminology equipment that allowed him to find links between crimes and calculate likely targets of criminals, and he also started a network of informants. While fulfilled at his work, he failed to have any successful romantic relationship, in his opinion because the women he was interested in, were unwilling to date a disabled man like he was. ===Bounty hunting collaboration with Spider-Woman: Initial activities and the Gamesmen=== thumb|left|McDowell collaborated with Spider-Woman as a bounty hunting team. Jessica Drew, also known as the superheroine Spider-Woman, had just moved to an apartment next door to his after she was evicted from her previous home during a bad streak that had left her unemployed and single. Trying to find out a new path for herself while making the most of her powers, she decided to make a partnership with McDowell to become a professional bounty hunter with McDowell's help. Spider-Woman approached McDowell willingly, asking him to help her become a professional crimefighter. McDowell found the criminals they targeted and organized Spider-Woman's activities to track them, giving her as much details as he could find using his means, and coordinated her activities sternly, but also worrying about her health and making sure she'd be OK. Although Spider-Woman was already active as a costumed adventurer, she had hidden her existence up to that point; from that moment, she was publicly known, although she did not try to obtain fame. Thus, Spider-Woman began to deal with McDowell's informers, including fireman-paramedic Hugh Donovan. More importantly, Spider-Woman dealt with LAPD Captain Alexander Walsh, who paid her the bounties using drop-boxes so that she did not need to reveal her identity to him. She did however reveal her identity to McDowell (or McDowell found it somehow). While this arrangement was fulfilling for both Spider-Woman and McDowell, he'd have loved to go to the field, which was infeasible due to his disability; and he also felt a crush towards Spider-Woman, which was not reciprocated, in his opinion because of his disability. thumb|left|McDowell prompted Spider-Woman to stop a serial killer. In some of their exploits as a team during the first weeks of their collaboration, McDowell correctly predicted that Lou DeFalco's criminal gang, for whom there was a reward, would attempt to rob the Majestic Jewelry Emporium; confident that they would be arrested, McDowell purchased new devices that he hoped to pay for with the reward. Spider-Woman apprehended DeFalco and his associates, and by then the reward for them had risen to $20,000. After that, McDowell studied the Shark Mob gang and concluded that they would take the Sandy Point Lighthouse to steal the gold cargo from the ship Regency III, which was passing nearby. Again, Spider-Woman defeated these enemies. Afterwards, McDowell prepared an elegant dinner for him and Spider-Woman, during which Spider-Woman recommended that he find a girlfriend, unaware that he was infatuated with Spider-Woman herself. In the following days, McDowell convinced Spider-Woman to chase the Killer Clown, a serial killer, even if there was no bounty for him. Spider-Woman successfully captured the Clown, and shortly thereafter captured five members of the Gamesman's gang who had stolen paintings from the Los Angeles County Art Museum, recovering the paintings in the process. thumb|left|Spider-Woman's romance with Braverman strained her professional relationship with McDowell. Understanding that Spider-Woman threatened his plans, the Gamesman began a plan to manipulate her through seduction: He had five of his goons attack her, and then the Gamesman, in his identity civilian of Tim Braverman, helped her escape. Pretending to be a Los Angeles Times reporter, Braverman courted Spider-Woman. Learning of this, McDowell first worried about the attack, and then distrusted Braverman, but Spider-Woman dismissed her concern, believing that McDowell was just jealous and had no right to interfere in her personal life. Even when McDowell verified that no one by the name of Braverman worked at the Times, Spider-Woman refused to stop seeing Braverman. While fulfilled at his work, he failed to have any successful romantic relationship, in his opinion because the women he was interested in, were unwilling to date a disabled man like he was. ===Bounty hunting collaboration with Spider-Woman: Initial activities and the Gamesmen=== thumb|left|McDowell collaborated with Spider-Woman as a bounty hunting team. Jessica Drew, also known as the superheroine Spider-Woman, had just moved to an apartment next door to his after she was evicted from her previous home during a bad streak that had left her unemployed and single. Trying to find out a new path for herself while making the most of her powers, she decided to make a partnership with McDowell to become a professional bounty hunter with McDowell's help. Spider-Woman approached McDowell willingly, asking him to help her become a professional crimefighter. McDowell found the criminals they targeted and organized Spider-Woman's activities to track them, giving her as much details as he could find using his means, and coordinated her activities sternly, but also worrying about her health and making sure she'd be OK. Although Spider-Woman was already active as a costumed adventurer, she had hidden her existence up to that point; from that moment, she was publicly known, although she did not try to obtain fame. Thus, Spider-Woman began to deal with McDowell's informers, including fireman-paramedic Hugh Donovan. More importantly, Spider-Woman dealt with LAPD Captain Alexander Walsh, who paid her the bounties using drop-boxes so that she did not need to reveal her identity to him. She did however reveal her identity to McDowell (or McDowell found it somehow). While this arrangement was fulfilling for both Spider-Woman and McDowell, he'd have loved to go to the field, which was infeasible due to his disability; and he also felt a crush towards Spider-Woman, which was not reciprocated, in his opinion because of his disability. thumb|left|McDowell prompted Spider-Woman to stop a serial killer. In some of their exploits as a team during the first weeks of their collaboration, McDowell correctly predicted that Lou DeFalco's criminal gang, for whom there was a reward, would attempt to rob the Majestic Jewelry Emporium; confident that they would be arrested, McDowell purchased new devices that he hoped to pay for with the reward. Spider-Woman apprehended DeFalco and his associates, and by then the reward for them had risen to $20,000. After that, McDowell studied the Shark Mob gang and concluded that they would take the Sandy Point Lighthouse to steal the gold cargo from the ship Regency III, which was passing nearby. Again, Spider-Woman defeated these enemies. Afterwards, McDowell prepared an elegant dinner for him and Spider-Woman, during which Spider-Woman recommended that he find a girlfriend, unaware that he was infatuated with Spider-Woman herself. In the following days, McDowell convinced Spider-Woman to chase the Killer Clown, a serial killer, even if there was no bounty for him. Spider-Woman successfully captured the Clown, and shortly thereafter captured five members of the Gamesman's gang who had stolen paintings from the Los Angeles County Art Museum, recovering the paintings in the process. thumb|left|Spider-Woman's romance with Braverman strained her professional relationship with McDowell. Understanding that Spider-Woman threatened his plans, the Gamesman began a plan to manipulate her through seduction: He had five of his goons attack her, and then the Gamesman, in his identity civilian of Tim Braverman, helped her escape. Pretending to be a Los Angeles Times reporter, Braverman courted Spider-Woman. Learning of this, McDowell first worried about the attack, and then distrusted Braverman, but Spider-Woman dismissed her concern, believing that McDowell was just jealous and had no right to interfere in her personal life. Even when McDowell verified that no one by the name of Braverman worked at the Times, Spider-Woman refused to stop seeing Braverman. However, Spider-Woman accepted McDowell's theory that the Gamesman would try to steal the Rajah Ruby from the Civic Auditorium, and prepared to protec
fields.personality: thumb|left|McDowell was infatuated with Spider-Woman. Scotty McDowell was a professional criminologist, dedicated, talented, and happy with his job, although he would have loved to join the FBI. His home was full of specialized equipment for his criminology work, and he was constantly improving it and buying new items. He also decorated the walls with wanted criminals posters. In his collaboration with Spider-Woman, McDowell primarily coordinated activities without participating in field work due to restrictions of the wheelchair, and instead defined where it was most appropriate to send Spider-Woman, both to patrol and to track down specific criminals. However, when Spider-Woman was in trouble, McDowell did not hesitate to leave the house as reinforcement, armed if necessary; although the violent field work clearly put him in danger, he demonstrated his courage and sang-froid on several occasions. Because he was wheelchair-confined, he had his home and car adapted, in addition to decorating both to his personal style. McDowell's walls were also adorned with paintings and a poster that could be from Conan the Barbarian. His well-stocked library included Random House Dictionary, and he occasionally read Playboy, although he was ashamed of it. McDowell was unable to maintain a romantic relationship to his satisfaction, and he believed that the ladies he was interested in, including Spider-Woman, were not interested in him due to his disability. Spider-Woman noticed that McDowell became jealous when she became interested in Tim Braverman and McDowell aggressively interrogated her. She never saw McDowell as anything but a friend. thumb|right|As the Hornet, McDowell was chauvinistic and arrogant. As the Hornet, McDowell became a macho vigilante who favored the use of force, even lethal force, against criminals, and said that women were not prepared to solve problems because they were much softer than "real men" like himself, so they should adapt to traditional gender roles (After being cured of the Hornet's powers and mind, McDowell confronted another criminal who supported traditional roles, Turner D. Century, and at no point did the sane McDowell suggested that he supported that, instead focusing on stopping Century). The Hornet did not care about collateral damage to innocent civilians, and was especially angry at Spider-Woman for several of her alleged sins against him: First, having shown false sympathy towards him because of his disability; then taking the glory of the job when he was doing the most difficult intellectual effort; and finally trying to use morality to prevent the Hornet from doing a good superhero job. Although the Hornet was strong, he was unable to defeat Spider-Woman because she was more cunning in combat; the Hornet only managed to escape her, repeatedly, by endangering innocents. After the second injection of Dr. Malus' drug, the Hornet became even more unstable, and although he could pretend to be McDowell, he aroused Spider-Woman's suspicions with various unusual behaviors (for example, calling him a new nickname, "Webdoll", which combined the typical nickname for her used by McDowell, "Web Lady", and the one used by the Hornet, "Dollface"), but she attributed it to the tension over McDowell's recent ordeal at the hands of the Enforcer. During the final confrontation, the Hornet became increasingly deranged, allowing Spider-Woman to defeat him and discover his identity. After recovering and leaving the Hornet persona behind, McDowell became increasingly demanding of Spider-Woman, insisting that she pursue more criminals and scolding her when she had found one of her targets and let him escape, even if it was because she was busy saving innocents. They both realized that they were developing different priorities: McDowell wanted to catch guilty people, and Spider-Woman wanted to help innocent people, and she thought that, no matter how good a person he was, he was becoming increasingly reluctant to consider alternative points of view to his own. Although they remained partners and friends, they argued more and more often, and she began to consider having a serious discussion on that topic. Finally, when McDowell was offered an appointment to the governor's crime commission, he decided to accept and asked Spider-Woman to end their partnership - at a time when Spider-Woman was already looking for a similar chance to move to another city.
powers: thumb|right|As the Hornet, McDowell could fly and was super-strong. McDowell only had superhuman powers during his brief stint as the Hornet. {{Navigation
equipment: as well as the technology to duplicate an I.D. card in a way that it can trick the computer sensors of a company like DRC, an untraceable phone line at his home, and a police radio.
weapons: McDowell had a handgun which he occasionally used, but was not a very good marksman.
fields.notes: Inconsistencies related to McDowell in the sources include: Most sources call this character "Scotty", including most of the comics and several non-comics, such as five handbooks published in the 21st century ( , Spider-Woman (Drew)'s profile; , Spider-Woman's profile; , Armadillo's profile; , Spider-Woman (Drew)'s profile; and , Dr. Karl Malus' profile). He is only called "Scott" in one comic ( , page 11, in which the narrator calls him Scott) and in four 20th-century handbooks ( , Jessica Drew's profile; , Dr. Karl Malus' profile; , Doctor Malus' profile; and , Spider-Woman I's profile). , Dr. Karl Malus' profile, says that Malus had first sent the Fly to the hospital to steal specialized equipment to be used in the process to restore the Fly's powers. However, in , Malus explicitly mentions the plan was for the Fly to kidnap Spider-Woman's known ally McDowell, at that time in a coma, to be used as a bait to attract her, so that they could get Spider-Woman's blood for a transfusion. Spider-Woman (Drew)'s profile, says that Malus "cured" McDowell from the Hornet's powers and derangement after Spider-Woman defeated Malus. However, in , the Werewolf defeats Malus, then McDowell recovers on his own because the powers were only temporary (as explained in , Dr. Karl Malus' profile) and he only needed to wash out the drugs from his body.
fields.trivia: Scotty nicknamed Spider-Woman "Web Lady", sometimes hyphenated as "Web-Lady" (but the spelling was kept coherent in all the mentions of her nickname in a given story); when not addressing her directly, he thought of her as "the Web Lady". The Hornet called her "Dollface." When Scotty called her "Web-Doll" (because he was secretly the Hornet at that point), Spider-Woman noticed the unusual nickname. Soon after Spider-Woman ended her partnership with McDowell, her new romantic interest David Ishima spontaneously called her "Weblady", but she didn't want anyone but McDowell to call her that. McDowell worked from his home, which is understandable due to his restricted mobility, even if he owned a car (with painted flames on the sides) that was adapted for him to drive and was not shy to leave his home. He had many specialized equipment for his criminology work, and decorated his walls with "Wanted" posters of criminals. McDowell occasionally sore saying "Holy Toledo." Jessica Drew's best friend at the time, Lindsay McCabe, apparently never met Scotty McDowell or heard Drew mentioning him - as McDowell was a known associate of Spider-Woman, not of Drew.

scout roberta.name: Scout (Roberta)
scout roberta.species: Human transformed by a stolen portion of the Power Cosmic
scout roberta.origin: Ever since she first learned of Galactus, a flourishing astronomer named Roberta wanted to become his Herald, and find a cure for his cosmic hunger. thumb|left|Regular form After stealing from Alicia Masters a statue of the Thing made with the essence of the Silver Surfer, Roberta absorbed it and gained a portion of the Surfer's Power Cosmic. Under the alias of Scout, Roberta tried to prove herself to Galactus in order to become his Herald, but to no avail. When Howard the Duck became a living Nexus of All Realities, Scout retrieved him from the clutches of the Stranger and gave him to Galactus, hoping her desired master would use him to travel to universes filled with unoccupied planets. Thus, Scout hoped to become the "ultimate" Herald, as she would have provided Galactus with infinite sources to appease his cosmic hunger. Unfortunately for Scout, when she brought Howard to Galactus, Galactus planned on making Howard his Herald instead of Scout. Scout was soon interrupted by the Silver Surfer who wished to retrieve Howard, as he did not deserve to be handled as an object to be exchanged. Scout later assisted the Silver Surfer confront the Collector for the existence of his prison planet, Collecton, and helped fend off the Elder of the Universe from Howard while he was using his power as the Nexus to teleport all of Collecton's prisoners back to their homes. After Howard was separated from the Nexus and used it on himself to go home, the Silver Surfer had a talk with Scout. He let her keep the Power Cosmic, and convinced her to stop pursuing Galactus any more. She decided instead to explore the cosmos in the search for a goal for herself, instead of helping Galactus achieve his own. Before beginning her journey, Scout decided to make sure Howard had made it to his destination safe, and visited him where he ended up, in Beverly Switzler's house in Maine, saving him from the attack of an Iron Punisher in the process. She subsequently gave Howard a lift to New York on her board, and gave him a sphere made of Power Cosmic that he could use if he ever needed help. When the nefarious Sparkitect Chipp stole the sphere from Howard to use its powers and escape from his superiors, Howard took advantage of the sphere's property as a calling card and summoned Scout. She appeared immediately on the scene and absorbed the Power Cosmic from Chipp, leaving him powerless.

screwbeard.name: Screwbeard
screwbeard.origin: Screwbeard was a Dwarf from the realm of Nidavellir and the Skornheim Mountains, and member of the Dynamite Dwarves. Screwbeard was recruited into the League of Realms, a team uniting warriors of the Nine Realms in order to hunt down Malekith the Accursed while he was slaughtering his people across the Nine Realms. That team was assembled as Thor desired to lead an army of Asgardians, but such action was considered an illegal incursion on the Realms. The team consisted of Sir Ivory Honeyshot of Alfheim, Ud the Troll, Lady Waziria of Svartalfheim and Oggy of Jotunheim. The League was first sent in Nidavellir to protect the Dark Elves' Queen in exile, Alflyse, but their inability to work together properly led to their inability to defend her. After that battle and the disastrous use he made of his dynamite, Thor took it from him. The League clashed with Malekith's forces multiple times, eventually managing to save refugees in Alfheim, slaughtering Dark Elves refugees, but once again Malekith slipped away. In order to prevent his League from falling apart in front of him, Thor had the group headed to the nearest tavern, where Thor and Ogg engaged in a drinking contest, while the others wagered on the winner, narrowly drinking the giant under the table. The next day, the League headed to Jotunheim where Malekith was hunting down a group of Elves who hided among the Mountain Giants. Oggy was directly targeted by the Accursed, who leaped into his mouth and brutally slashed apart the Giant's brain with his blades, felling him. Having gone to the Frost Giants for help, Malekith was out of reach of the League of Realms. Enraged, the others had to hold Thor back to prevent an incursion inside the Frost Giants territory and a larger conflict. After burying Oggy, the League went to Vanaheim and found more Elves dead, slain fighting amongst themselves. Thor realized that there was to be a traitor in their midst. Thor cast a spell and, accusing Ud of being the traitor, seemingly executed him against the League's decision. Ud was transported elsewhere in Vanaheim with a note addressed to the League pinned to his backside and leading them to the Midgard location of the Dark Elves refugees. That rash action caused the league to split, with only Lady Waziria as companion to Thor. While the two of them headed to Midgard to find the Council of the Unhallowed, the Dark Elf ruling council in hiding, and urged them to unite against Malekith, the rest of the League found Ud, as confused as them. Back in Midgard, Thor accused Waziria of being a traitor as Malekith had followed them to the butcher shop. Enraged, she blasted Thor with a mystical bolt, resulting in a strange creature wrenching itself from inside of Thor, revealing that Malekith had been ahead of the League all along by bugging Thor. The League then showed up with Ud. As Screwbeard was about to killed by his own dynamite stabbed into his hand by Scumtongue (whom he was defying), Ud saved him by cutting his hand off. Alongside with Thor and the Dark Elves, they took down Malekith, but the fight was stopped by the Council decision to have him their king. When Thor had his arm cut off, Screwbeard brought him a gift from the Dwarves of Nidavellir requested by Odin, a prosthetic arm made of Black Uru.
abilities: Demolitions: Screwbeard is an expert in the use of explosives.
weapons: Dynamite sticks. Used a candy cane once.

scrier cosmic being.name: Scrier (Cosmic Being)
scrier cosmic being.origin: Scrier claimed to be a being older than the universe and the several universes that occurred before the current one. He claimed to have been old when Galactus was young. Scrier met with Agatha Harkness over five centuries before the fall of Atlantis, circa 18,500 BC. He was believed to have been destroyed circa this period. Scrier is a being of immense power with nebulous goals. He frequently works through agents, many of whom are unaware he is pulling their strings. He is the inspiration for the several millennial old cabal of the Brotherhood of the Scriers. He was awakened from his eternal slumber in a temple in the Himalayas by the Silver Surfer. He temporarily returned Silver Surfer's repressed emotions to him and tasked him with stealing a child named Edward Cross from his drug addicted mother, but Silver Surfer eventually chose not to, despite this the Scrier secreted away the child and his mother for unknown reasons. Scrier and Agatha Harkness later helped Silver Surfer deal with his infection at the hands of The Other. Scrier would then do battle with Adam K'ad-Mon for control over the Nexus of All Realities. He claimed that the whole affair may have been a feint to insure that he merged with Ellen Sallis. Later, the Other and Scrier renewed their conflict and tricked Thor into sacrificing himself to the Other to ensure a half billion year peace accord between Scrier and the Other. Galactus disrupted this plan, but Scrier hinted this may have been his intent all along.
powers: Limitless Cosmic Power

scrounger.origin: While scrounging in a ruined building, the self-styled Scrounger found the Controller trapped under the debris. The Scrounger fell under his control and provided him with the little help he could manage, such as food. The Controller then used the Scrounger as his minion to distribute slave discs. Iron Man defeated the Controller and his other minions, the Blood Brothers; as the Controller's exoskeleton failed and rendered him paralyzed, the Scrounger took the Controller away and started taking care of him again.
weaknesses: The Scrounger was weak-willed: The Controller controlled him without his slave discs.

sculpture.name: Sculpture
sculpture.species: Large statue that had been brought to life
sculpture.origin: The Stone Man was the creation of a Nazi sculptor named Lubitch and a Nazi scientist named Professor Schultz who wanted to create an unbeatable weapon for Nazi Germany. Attempting to bring their sculpture to life, the Professor's machines overloaded and exploded killing the two men but bringing the statue to life. Loyal to Nazi Germany, the statue came across an army of British soldiers who came to destroy a Nazi ammunition factory. The creature slaughtered the entire troop except for one soldier who was saved by the Destroyer. The Destroyer fought the creature to a standstill, causing it to flee from him in fear. The creature came across a group of Nazi soldiers, whose commanding officer recruited the creature upon learning that it was loyal to the Nazi cause and upon hearing news that the Destroyer was in the area. Patrolling the ammunition factory, the statue came across the surviving British soldier holding a number of Nazi troops at gunpoint and attacked him. The creature then rushed to the factory just as the Destroyer was overpowered and captured. The creature confronted its enemy in the dungeon, where the Destroyer told it that he had planted a bomb that would destroy the factory, taking them both with it. Fearing this, the statue attempted to flee, smashing through the door. The lone British soldier, on death's door, then freed the Destroyer. The Destroyer escaped just as the building exploded, destroying the statue with it.
powers: Made of stone, the statue has super-human strength and durability.

scumtongue.name: Scumtongue
scumtongue.origin: ===Origin=== Scumtongue was one of the Dark Elves of Svartalfheim loyal to Malekith the Accursed. ===The Great Niffleheim Escape=== In order to help him return, as Malekith was then imprisoned into the Hall of Nastrond, in the frozen land of Hel, on Niffleheim, Scumtongue, Sourfoot and two other Dark Elves approached a wizard who brew them a potion (possibly composed of Faerie blood) who would prevent detection from Hela and her Valkyries, and slew that wizard once his work was done. Scumtongue was wounded early during the fight by the Spiders of Hel, guardians of the Nastrond Prison, but when Malekith was freed and all the Spiders killed, he was the only survivor of the commando. ===Svartalfheim Civil War=== ====The Svartalfheim Massacre==== Scumtongue then took part in the terror campaign of Malekith, joined by more loyalist and the Wild Hunt, slaughtering the Dark Elf Dove Gut tribe and escaping the wrath of Thor, Sif and the Warriors Three who intervened on the massacre site. ====Nidavellir==== He then participated in the massacre of Alflyse and her court, as they were hiding under the Dwarves' protection in the Skornheim Mountains, and escaped again Thor, now leading the Congress of Worlds-mandated League of Realms, when League member Screwbeard threw explosives all over the place. ====Jotunheim==== Later, three days after the failed attack on a refugee camp in Alfheim, they attacked other Dark Elves in the Brown Alps of Jotunheim, where they hid like mice in the walls of the Mountain Giants' cabins. Slaughtering those refugees, the Dark Elves were attacked again by the League of Realms. Malekith dragged them into Frost Giants' territory, killed League member Oggy, and had Scumtongue blow a horn to attract their Frost Giant allies. Despite Thor's rage, Sir Ivory forced the League to retreat to avoid an act of war against the Frost Giants. Malekith and Scumtongue then retreated into Utgard. ====Council of the Unhallowed==== As Thor had asked for the Council of the Unhallowed to gather and assemble the Dark Elves around one leader, Scumtongue and Malekith arrived, informed by a bug planted inside Thor by a Dark Elf a long time ago. Screwbeard, holding a grudge against Scumtongue, searched for him during the battle. Scumtongue stabbed his hand (holding a dynamite stick) to the wall while Screwbeard threw acid at his face. Screwbeard was saved by fellow League member Ud the Troll who cut off his hand, and the fight resumed, until the Council decided to appoint Malekith as their new king. ===Senator Scumtongue=== Right after the anointment of Malekith as King of Svartalfheim and Lord Protector of all Dark Elves, Senator Volstagg informed him that to obtain approval from the Congress of Worlds and peace between worlds, he had to offer one of his court as emissary and representative. Scumtongue was consequently made senator at the Congress of Worlds. During the beginning of the War of the Realms, when Malekith's Dark Elves invaded Alfheim, Scumtongue's fellow Svartalfheim senator refuted the claims from the Light Elf Senator Milkmane. Following Malekith's death and the end of the War of the Realms, Scumtongue holded up in Svartalfheim holding hostage one of the missing Norns. The League of Realms were deployed to save his hostage.
weapons: Ice Saber
weaknesses: Scumtongue is mute.

scuttlebutt stacy.name: Scuttlebutt Stacy
scuttlebutt stacy.origin: "Scuttlebutt" Stacy was an American soldier who fought in the Korean War during the 1950s. He earned his nickname due to his constant gossip and chatter. He frequently fought with his fellow soldier Sargent Rock Murdock. In the pair's earliest recorded appearance, they uncovered a plot by communist soldiers to use sickles to steal rice from a nearby Korean farming community, and prevented them from stealing the rice the local villagers desperately needed.
weapons: Those typically wielded by Marine during the Korean War

scylla hydra.name: Scylla (Hydra)
scylla hydra.origin: The being that became known as Scylla was a Hydra experiment codenamed "Project: Scylla", whose intent was to create a human hybrid that could exist in the depths of the ocean. After it's creation in an secret underwatercraft, the experiment ran wild and killed the crew of the ship, which sank to the bottom of the sea, where it lay for an undisclosed amount of time. Nick Fury heard of Scylla and sent Iron Man down to stabilize the ship from falling into a trench in order to retrieve Scylla. Against Fury's wishes, Iron Man entered the craft and found Scylla who attacked him while asking for help. A short battle ensued where the craft was slowly knocked into the trench, forcing Iron Man to flee as the ship crashed to the depths. Unbeknownst the Iron Man and Fury, Scylla survived and fled deeper into the ocean.

scytalis.name: Scytalis
scytalis.species: Human mutate (Russian Super-Soldier; later corrupted by the Chronoserpent
scytalis.first_appearance: Marvel Realm of Champions: Elegy Season 1 2
scytalis.origin: ===Origin=== Black Widow was infected by the Chronoserpent, transforming her into Scytalis. ===Elegy=== Scytalis was present alongside Bahamet when Anathi was taken to the Chronoserpent by Glykhan. She then witnessed Anathi receiving the Infinity Claw from Black Panther and using it to free herself from the Chronoserpent. ===Contest of Champions: Book 2=== At some point following the destruction of Battleworld, Scytalis worked with Ouroboros. Under the guise of Black Widow, she infiltrated the Avengers and wedged them against Carina Tivan. While on an investigation, Civil Warrior decrypted information from an Ouroboros bunker that someone named Scytalis had infiltrated the Avengers. Without any leads as to who it could be, Carina conjured a plan to draw out Scytalis by having the Summoner and Civil Warrior stand in as Captain America and Iron Man respectively. Leading the disguised duo to a safe room in Avengers Tower, Carina warned them of a traitor among the Avengers. Upon Carina's exit, the tower's security systems went haywire and sealed the safe room from the rest of the building, locking "Captain America" and "Iron Man" inside. Black Widow revealed herself to them and her intent to splinter the Avengers by staging their two founding leaders killing each other. When the illusion around the Summoner and Civil Warrior fizzled away, Scytalis shed her disguise and retaliated. The safe room was breached open as the rest of the Avengers and Carina witnessed Scytalis' defeat against the Summoner. As a final gambit, Scytalis self-destructed and blew up the room but was thwarted by Civil Warrior, who used a protective field to save everyone.
powers: Skill Class Champion: As a Skill Champion, Scytalis has an advantage over Science Class champions in the Contest of Champions. Spider Arms: Scytalis has four spider arms that can be summoned from her back.
weaknesses: Mutant Class Champions: Scytalis is considered a Skill Class Champion under the Contest, weakening her against Mutant Class Champions.

scythe lost generation.name: Scythe (Lost Generation)
scythe lost generation.origin: Not much has been revealed about the history and origin of Scythe. Presumably he had a long criminal/mercenary career, at times teaming up or otherwise associating with villains such as Blackjack and Chimera. One of his later recorded activities included acceptance of a mercenary job to sabotage the 1963 moon landing. The plot was masterminded by the alien Skrulls, who hoped to subjugate Earth at some point, and brought Scythe and the other mercenaries to the moon via their own spaceship, where the group was confronted by the hero team known as the First Line. Scythe and the aliens were defeated, and he was remanded into custody. His ultimate fate remains to be revealed.
weapons: Scythe wielded two scythe-like blades.

scythian algurus.name: Scythian Algurus
scythian algurus.origin: Scythian was a remorseless and destructive deity of the planet Dartayus in the Negative Zone. At one point in Dartayus' early history, he was magically turned into stone. The area around his body became the Kavangian Plateau, holy ground to his followers, at the emplacement of the Temple of Scythian. Scythian's true nature and fate was confined to ancient text while more modern holy books apparently presented him was a much more remorseful presence. His religion became long-dead, and he was known as the Fallen God until, in modern times, dissident Kologoth Antares preached about him in order to obtain followers for himself. The Temple of Scythian served as headquarters to Kologoth's Dartayus Union. After studying more about Scythian through the ancient texts, Kologoth learned of a way to set him free from his imprisonment, and set out to do so to use Scythian as the instrument of vengeance against the world that made him an outcast. Kologoth's forces were in the middle of a battle against the X-Men when Scythian was awaken and began to rampage through Dartayus. Since magic was no longer in use in the planet, there was no way to turn him back into stone. Instead, the X-Men used a ship to tow Scythian into the deadly vortex located in the center of the Negative Zone, ridding of him. Scythian's restrainment was short-lived, and he eventually escaped from the vortex. Fueled by a thirst for revenge against the X-Men, Scythian ripped a hole in the fabric of the Negative Zone and emerged in the space between Jupiter and Saturn. He made his way to Earth and landed on Paris. Captain Britain and Meggan engaged the creature before the X-Men arrived to the scene. Most of the heroes attacked Scythian with the intent to weaken him while Magik conjured a stepping disc to send him to Limbo. Scythian was finally defeated when Kitty Pryde crashed the Blackbird into his back, and the strength of the impact pushed him into Magik's portal.

sean benard.name: Sean Benard
sean benard.origin: Sean Benard worked as a police officer at the Vancouver Police Department. Sean was in a very sticky situation when he met the man named Logan. He had just gunned down two of his fellow officers who had turned crooked, using the last of his bullets and was faced with the third who had a shotgun. Logan took out the gunman without killing him and escorted Sean to Ottawa, where he woke the Prime Minister and had him draft Sean into the Canadian secret service. Sean was escorted to the Flight Ranch where he met some rather unusual people and underwent extensive training by Dr Langkowski, until he finally met James Hudson and found out why he was there. He had been recruited as a member of Canada's official super team, known as the Flight. Using a suit of armor that Hudson had designed for planetary exploration, he was given the code name Groundhog. thumb|left|200px|Groundhog On the Flight's first mission, to stop Egghead from launching a nuclear payload into New York City, many things went wrong: Smart Alec broke under the pressure, Wolverine could barely control himself and Saint Elmo had to sacrifice himself in order to save his friends. Sean left, disgruntled, telling Hudson, "If you want someone to wear that suit so badly, have the courage of your convictions -- and wear it yourself!" Charges were never laid against Benard for the killing of his fellow-policemen. He was last seen watching the unveiling of Alpha Flight.
abilities: Highly skilled police officer, trained in hand-to-hand combat and small weapons.

sean boyle.name: Sean Boyle
sean boyle.origin: Sean Boyle wore a Spider-Man mask while mugging and so came to be nicknamed the "Spider-Mugger". After mugging Peter Parker, he discovered Spider-Man's Web-Shooters. Boyle deduced that his victim was Spider-Man. Boyle had surrendered the credit cards he stole to an employer and was killed when attempting to retrieve Parker's to learn the identity and home address of Spider-Man. His body was then dumped in an alley where Spider-Man discovered him and was accused by police officers of having killed him.

sean cassidy moira vii 1.name: Sean Cassidy (Moira-VII.1)
sean cassidy moira vii 1.species: Mutant bonded with the Spirit of Variance
sean cassidy moira vii 1.origin: ===Sins of Sinister=== ====Year 10==== While refuging at the Sanctum Sanctorum, Vox Ignis was attacted by the Legion of the Night. He managed to be use his Scream of Change on some of them, and converted Wagnerine, Wallcrawler and Auntie Fortune to his cause. The Legion of the Night became a group of Mother Righteous' followers and started stealing weapons and magical artifacts for her. When Mother Righteous's actions cause the death of Wallcrawler, Vox Ignis started doubting her methods. ====Year 100==== Vox Ignis spent years continuing to search for Nightkin that he could free and bring over to Mother Righteous' service, while the Sinisters destroyed virtually every opposition in the galaxy. Through the years he accompanied Mother Righteous as she visited various people, asking them what they would have done differently. After learning the troubles of the Nightkin from Wagnerine, he helped her convinced Mother Righteous to free the original Nightcrawler and Dr. Nemesis. When the rabid Nightcrawler attacked Mother Righteous for corrupting his idea of the spark, she killed him. When an angered Wagnerine attempted to kill Mother Righteous in revenge, she ordered Vox Ignis to kill her. He hesitated for a moment, prompting Mother Righteous to punish him and Wagnerine to flee, now knowing that Mother Righteous had stolen her infant daughter and made her a part of the reliquary. ====Year 1000==== Still in service to Mother Righteous, Vox Ignis was sent to find Galactus, who had become infested with Spirits of Vengeance. Hoping to ally with them, he found that the spirits still abhored the Spirit of Variance. He spent 56 years fleeing Galactus, and upon receiving word from Mother Righteous brought him to the World Farm where the Moira Engine was housed. To his shock, Mother Righteous had planned all this from the start, and had placed Galactus right in the path of the Juggernaut, who had been fired as a bullet into space nearly 1000 years before. Juggernaut killed Galactus, and together with the sacrifice of every Nightkin, Mother Righteous was finally free to enter the World Farm. Here, she revealed the truth of the Reliquary Perilous; that it was not a weapon intended to fix the universe, but instead a way for her to send her knowledge and memories of this timeline backwards to her past self when the timeline was ultimately reset due to the Moira clone's death. In addition, she separated the Spirit of Variance from Banshee, adding it to the reliquary. Before she could complete her schemes, Wagnerine arrived to kill her and free her daughter. Banshee betrayed her, and though he was too old and frail to even use his sonic scream, he distracted her long enough for Wagnerine to kill her. As Wagnerine left, Sean was shocked to see Moira appear. She suddenly shot him, and claimed the reliquary for herself.
weapons: Ghost Rider's Chain: As Vox Ignis, Sean used a version of the chain wielded by the Ghost Riders.

sean collins.name: Sean Collins
sean collins.species: Presumably Mutant; Believed falsely to be Homo ultima
sean collins.origin: Sean Collins was the first child born on Avalon, the space station where Magneto assembled the mutants to ascend out of Earth. Born from the Acolytes Rusty Collins and Skids, Sean's genetic make-up readings were magnetically modified by Magneto in order to lure Hank McCoy and unite his fellow mutants, as a rift was forming in his community. The X-Factor analysis "revealed" that, at maturity, Sean would be able to alter his mutation at will, enabling him to choose himself his powers and therefore, he was part of an evolutionary jump as big from the mutants than was the jump of mutants from Humans, and could be the next step, Homo ultima, the ultimate being. While his parents were joyed by the news, McCoy expressed his doubts about what to think of it. Scanner learned the intel and soon reported it to the Acolytes "Annihilist faction" (in favor of taking Earth from the humans) and to their leader Fabian Cortez who feared that Homo ultima would turn against Homo superior and take Earth for themselves. In the same way, Milan informed Exodus who expressed same concerns. The two Acolytes factions sought the counsel of Magneto, who let them decide together what should be done, and they agreed on a truce, time to terminate the baby, with less opposition among their ranks. The Acolytes intercepted McCoy, Skids and Rusty while they were intending to exit the station with a space shuttle. Although Beast and the couple fought bravely, they were unable to prevent Amelia Voght from reluctantly asphyxiating the baby, immediately asking forgiveness for her actions and claiming "it was self-defense". Once Sean dead, the couple and Beast decided to leave forever the station, while the Acolytes granted gratitude to them, considering that their baby had been a warning for mutantkind and that they will unite to survive this threat. Days later, Colossus decided to leave at his turn, but not before consulting Magnus who admitted his actions, regrets and explained it. Peter left then, warning Magneto about the fact his lies might turn to be true one day.

sean dolan.name: Sean Dolan
sean dolan.origin: thumb|left|150px|Sean Dolan Sean Dolan was once the squire of the Black Knight. He somehow got ahold of the Ebony Blade and traveled around as a drifter until he decided to help repair the recently destroyed Slorenia. In Slorenia he was decided to draw the blade. As a result the souls of the deceased Slorenians were harvested into the blade turning him into the Bloodwraith. The Bloodwraith seemed unstoppable and could not be destroyed. The Avengers could not defeat him. The Scarlet Witch instead strengthened his bond to Slorenia, not only linking him to the people but to the borders as well, trapping him inside.
abilities: Could harness the power of the dead
weapons: Ebony Blade, formerly used the Earth-374 version as Black Wraith
weaknesses: Can not travel outside Slorenia's borders

fields.notes: The Bloodwraith appears to be a separate entity that takes over Sean Dolan's body whenever he holds the unsheathed Ebony Blade. While the Bloodwraith is active on the Earthly plane, Dolan's soul exists within an ethereal realm of darkness within the blade and can sometimes exert an influence on the Bloodwraith's actions. Dolan is the only person who has been observed to be transformed in that way by the Ebony Blade. Although the Bloodwraith entity is clearly connected to the sword, its origin has yet to be revealed.

sean dunne.name: Sean Dunne
sean dunne.origin: Sean Dunne led a team of IRA terrorists who carried out an attack at Heathrow Airport in an unsuccessful attempt to kill Scotland Yard inspector John Bartlett, but which resulted in the deaths of innocent people. He managed to escape after the attack and hide in a safe house in London, which was revealed to Spider-Man by another terrorist whom he had knocked out and later interrogated in prison. In the hideout, together with other IRA terrorists, they attempted to organize a bomb attack on the British Parliament during a speech by Margaret Thatcher, an attack that was almost foiled by the intervention of Scotland Yard and MI-5, who stormed the terrorists' hideout, secretly aided by Spider-Man, who knocked out two terrorists, but Dunne and others managed to escape. Spider-Man later figured out what Dunn and the other terrorists were trying to do, namely to blow up the foundations of the British Parliament itself, so he sneaked into the London sewers beneath the British Parliament and stopped the attempt to detonate the dynamite by pulling the detonator wires, but Dunn threw a grenade so that the explosion would still trigger the dynamite. Spider-Man intercepted the grenade by trapping it to the wall with his web. Dunn tried to pull the grenade off the wall, but it exploded, causing him to lose an arm and an eye. Seriously injured, he was captured by the authorities.

sean madigan.name: Sean Madigan
sean madigan.species: Human cyborg; reanimated skull and brain in a tank attached to a robot body.
sean madigan.origin: thumb|left|250px|Original appearance Sean was the son of George Tarleton, born after his mother Linda had an affair with him in college and who abandoned her when he learned she was pregnant. George would go on to join A.I.M. and become M.O.D.O.K. years later. When Sean grew up he joined A.I.M. himself and learned who his father was. Angry at having been abandoned by his father he began plotting from within A.I.M. and worked to undermine and destabilize them, to destroy what his father loved instead of him. To this end he retrieved a bomb that could destabilize DNA, claiming to some parts of A.I.M. that he would use it to stabilize his father and to others that he would use it to kill him. Once he had the device and his father he installed in his father's chair and was going to detonate the bomb in Times Square. The superhero Ms. Marvel (Carol Danvers) and her Lightning Storm team had become aware of his actions and background thanks to information provided by Monica Rappaccini. Ms. Marvel flew his father out of range when the device detonated and informed her that he knew what Sean was up to. Believing his father was dead, Sean carried on with his plan and broadcast to A.I.M across multiple worlds and encouraged them to splinter apart, but before he could finish his broadcast, he was shot in the head by Monica Rappaccini. His skull and brain were saved and preserved by A.I.M. agents from one of the many now fractured cells and reanimated, stored within a jar and attached to a robotic body.

sean madrox.name: Sean Madrox
sean madrox.species: Son of mutant duplicate; (seemingly dupe himself)
sean madrox.origin: ===Conception and Gestation=== After celebrating with copious libations, one night Jamie Madrox spent the night with both Siryn and M; at the same time in two different locations. Madrox unwittingly created a dupe (or two), which allowed him to sleep with both women. After reabsorbing the dupe(s), Madrox was left with a hazy understanding of what happened and two furious women. Not long after that night, Siryn discovered that she was pregnant. Although the conception was far from normal, Siryn's pregnancy went relatively smoothly with few problems. ===Birth and Absorption=== While in active labor, Siryn proposed and Madrox accepted. After a few hours labor, Siryn gave birth to a healthy baby boy and was able to share the experience with her friends and teammates from X-Factor. She decided to name the infant Sean, after her late father Sean Cassidy. This was also the first time she really admitted her father was dead; a trauma with which she was still dealing. thumb|200px|left|Madrox absorbing Sean However, just hours after his birth, Madrox held baby Sean and involuntarily absorbed him. Despite Madrox's efforts to stop and his mother's screams, Sean slowly disappeared into his father just like any other dupe. Siryn, filled with rage toward Jamie, broke his finger and told him to leave. thumb|250px|left|Madrox absorbing Sean Madrox later theorized that a dupe had actually slept with Siryn, not himself. Furthermore, the son of a duplicate is itself also a duplicate. As such, when Sean came into physical contact with Madrox Prime, he was absorbed just like any other dupe. Sean's short life had terrible and lasting effect on his parents, both of whom fell into deep depressions after his death.
powers: Sean potentially had the ability of Kinetic Duplication like Madrox and his dupes, but he never demonstrated this power.

sean watanabe.name: Sean Watanabe
sean watanabe.origin: Sean Watanabe was trained in the martial arts by his father Yuji. In competition Sean always seemed to know his opponent's next move. He joined the military and became a member of the Navy SEAL's. He was given the nickname of Brass for taking on the tough jobs. After he ended his military service, Sean met a woman named Theresa, whom he planned to marry. However, they were near Avengers Mansion, which was attacked by the Mandarin during the 'Acts of Vengeance' conspiracy. Theresa fled into the street during the confusion and was struck by a car. Angry, Sean vowed he would go after all responsible. He started by attacking the Mandarin's operations in Chinatown. Deathwatch sent his men looking for all allies of Dan Ketch and the Ghost Rider. seaweed man.name: Seaweed Man
seaweed man.origin: ===Guardian of the Cave=== As part of his ongoing quest to recover Neptune's enchanted trident, Sub-Mariner was tasked with venturing into Cave of Shadows. However, before he could claim the legendary weapon, he first had to overcome a formidable guardian—the monstrous Seaweed Man. Namor quickly realised that he was outmatched in sheer strength and endurance, as the creature’s tangled, sinewy form made it nearly impervious to direct attacks. Instead of engaging it in prolonged combat, the Sub-Mariner relied on his superior speed and tactical prowess. He swam in rapid circles around the Seaweed Man, creating a powerful vortex that ensnared and immobilised the creature just long enough for him to slip into the cave. There, Namor recovered the next crucial clue in his quest before making his escape, leaving the Seaweed Man trapped in the swirling waters behind him. ===Dire Wraiths=== Sometime later the monstrous Seaweed Man lay dormant in the ocean depths, until a sinister faction of Dire Wraith sorceresses uncovered its resting place. As part of their broader scheme to conquer Earth, the Wraiths sought to claim Atlantis as a strategic stronghold. To accomplish this, they planned to harness the Seaweed Man’s immense latent power. Using an enchanted Black Pearl, they amplified their own dark magic and began a ritual to awaken the ancient sleeper. However, their plans did not go unnoticed. Both Rom, the Spaceknight, and Namor, the Sub-Mariner, arrived separately but swiftly recognised the greater threat at hand. Though the two warriors initially clashed, they quickly realised they shared a common enemy. Before they could intervene, several of the Dire Wraiths, realising they could not win through conventional means, sacrificed themselves, transferring their dark energies into the Pearl. The ritual’s final surge of power succeeded in fully awakening the Seaweed Man, but with an unintended consequence—the infusion of corrupt magic had transformed it into a rampaging force of destruction. Now more powerful than ever, the Seaweed Man ignored both Namor and Rom, setting its sights directly on Atlantis. As the massive creature advanced, the city's defenses proved woefully ineffective against its enchanted, ever-shifting form. Realising that brute force alone would not stop the monster, Namor recalled his earlier victory over it. He convinced Rom to aid him in recreating an even larger vortex, hoping to subdue it once more. However, the Seaweed Man, now bolstered by dark magic, proved far more resistant than before. Seeing no other option, Rom unleashed a sustained barrage of energy blasts from his Neutralizer, targeting the creature’s magical core. As the blasts drained its supernatural essence, the vortex at last took full effect, tearing the creature apart. The once-monstrous Seaweed Man was reduced to nothing more than harmless strands of seaweed, adrift in the ocean currents. Or so it seemed… but, as some whispered, the darkness that had infused it might still linger, waiting for another opportunity to rise again.

sebastian.name: Sebastian
sebastian.origin: Sebastian is a college student from Chicago who became a member of a gang of Mutants known as the Ghosts of Cyclops, who justified their violent attacks claiming to follow the legacy of the deceased Cyclops. Cyclops' time-displaced younger counterpart started tracking the Ghosts of Cyclops, and discovered a pattern to their attacks, so he was able to be present during their following appearance. The Ghost appeared and started scaring people, and the young Cyclops confronted them until the police arrived and they fled. After the confrontation the young Cyclops was able to track him down to Algar University. When he entered the facility, two of the members of the Ghost recognized him and alerted their boss. They put on their masks, confronted him in the library and began to beat him ending with the police arresting the young Cyclops and Thirst leader of the cyclops ghosts. While in custody, the rest of the Cyclops Phantasms came to Thirst's rescue, swiftly subduing the officers at the facility. However, when they tried to escape, they found themselves surrounded by dozens of S.W.A.T. When they decided to fight their way through the cops, the X-Men arrived and fought them. Both mutant teams ended up surrounded by officers, and Thirst tried to convince his teammates to keep fighting. When a cop ordered to open fire at the Ghost of Cyclops, the young Cyclops projected an energy blast in the space between them to get their attention, and gave a speech that convinced the officers to act non-lethally. Her current status is unknown.
